findingsSummary: Core hardening solid: path containment (dir_fd anchoring), ownership (secure_stat), no-follow (O_NOFOLLOW on all opens), atomic writes, temp safety, fail-open default all verified. 5 P2 advisories: full env passed to subprocess, TOCTOU in advance() poison, helperPath follows symlinks, POSIX-only with no platform detection, cwd-derived project hash. CHK-030/031/033/130/132 verified.
noveltyJustification: 5 new P2 findings (weighted=5). Accumulated weighted total ~15. Ratio 0.33 reflects that core hardening is proven solid — new findings are edge-case refinements, not gap discoveries. No P0 or P1 found.
ruledOut: P0: Symlink injection — O_NOFOLLOW on all opens, ISLNK check on base
P0: Path traversal escape — dir_fd anchoring prevents escape
P0: Unchecked ownership — secure_stat on all ops
P0: TOCTOU check/use — dir_fd anchoring + atomic rename + post-rename stat
P1: Temp file residue — finally block + bounded cleanup
P1: State dir permission bypass — 0o700 + secure_stat mode check

title: Full process environment passed to Python subprocess — least-privilege violation
scopeProof: rg -n "process\.env" directive-lifecycle-file-store.ts shows only line 132 and line 46. The helper only reads SPECKIT_DIRECTIVE_STORE_TEST_PAUSE_MS from env (store.py:358).
recommendation: Pass a minimal environment object with only PATH, HOME, and SPECKIT_DIRECTIVE_STORE_TEST_PAUSE_MS instead of process.env.

claimAdjudication.claim: Passing full process.env to a spawned Python subprocess is a least-privilege violation that could expose secrets
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the Python script needs any env vars beyond TEST_PAUSE_MS — it does not. Also checked if spawned process isolation prevents env leakage — spawnSync passes the env struct directly to the OS process.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The Python helper is a trusted same-project script executed by the same user; env exposure is a defense-in-depth concern, not an active exploit path. The subprocess is short-lived (750ms timeout, then SIGKILL).
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Same-user dependency, short-lived subprocess, fail-open default

title: TOCTOU between spawn result and failsafe poison in advance()
scopeProof: rg -n "advance\(\)|mark-poison|clear-poison|failsafe_poisoned" directive-lifecycle-file-store.ts directive-lifecycle-store.py shows only this code path.
recommendation: Collapse the poison clear/mark into the same Python invocation as the advance operation to avoid the TOCTOU window.

claimAdjudication.claim: advance() has a TOCTOU window between the spawn result and the failsafe poison call that can cause incorrect poison state
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Considered whether flock(LOCK_EX) makes advance and separate poison clear/mark atomic — separate spawnSync() calls with separate Python processes, each acquiring their own lock, so not atomic.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: Fail-open to full delivery is the safe default; incorrect poison state degrades suppression but never causes incorrect suppression. Narrow race window.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Both failure modes result in full delivery (safe default); neither enables stale/incorrect suppression.

title: helperPath() uses existsSync which follows symlinks — no integrity verification
scopeProof: rg -n "existsSync|helperPath" directive-lifecycle-file-store.ts shows this is the only path-resolution mechanism for the helper.
recommendation: Add a stat check to verify the resolved file is a regular file (not a symlink), or verify a hash/signature of the Python helper before spawning.

claimAdjudication.claim: helperPath() follows symlinks via existsSync with no integrity check, enabling helper substitution
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked if the project's .gitignore or file permissions prevent symlink planting — they do not. Attacker needs write access to the project directory.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: Write access to the project directory implies existing code execution capability. The helper substitution vector doesn't increase the attack surface.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Requires existing write access to the project directory — equivalent to existing code execution.

title: Python store helper fails POSIX-only operations silently on non-POSIX platforms — no platform detection
scopeProof: rg -n "fcntl|O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY|flock" directive-lifecycle-store.py shows pervasive POSIX dependency. rg -n "platform|posix|windows|darwin" shows no matches.
recommendation: Add an explicit platform check at the top of main() that exits cleanly on non-POSIX platforms, or document in ENV-REFERENCE.md that durable suppression requires a POSIX platform.

claimAdjudication.claim: Python store helper uses POSIX-only syscalls with no platform detection — silent failure on Windows
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked if the TS wrapper has a platform check before spawning — it does not. ImportError for fcntl at module level would be caught by main() try/except (store.py:372-376).
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: On Windows, import fcntl would raise ImportError, caught by the top-level try/except, returning ok: false. TS wrapper returns null → full delivery. Fail-open safety is preserved.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Fail-open design handles non-POSIX gracefully — import fcntl fails → ok: false → full delivery. No security bypass on Windows.

title: cwd-derived project hash partitions state silently across working directories
scopeProof: rg -n "getcwd|cwd.*process\.cwd" directive-lifecycle-store.py directive-lifecycle-file-store.ts shows these are the only project-isolation mechanics.
recommendation: Derive the project hash from a stable, workspace-root-relative path rather than cwd.

claimAdjudication.claim: cwd-derived project hash causes state partitioning when working directory changes
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked if the hook execution environment guarantees a stable CWD — it does not. State fragmentation results in full delivery (safe default).
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: State is disposable — losing suppression state results in full delivery, which is the safe default. Partition is preferable to cross-project collision.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: State partition = full delivery (safe default). No cross-project leakage possible. Primarily an operational surprise, not a security flaw.

detail: REQ-P1-003 NFR-S01 verified: path containment (store.py:44-85), ownership (store.py:38-41), no-follow (store.py:50,90,128), size bounds (store.py:14-15), atomic writes (store.py:139-145)

CHK-030 [P0]: dir_fd anchoring verified. CHK-031 [P0]: owner/mode/link-count/type/size/schema rejection verified. CHK-033 [P1]: bounded temp cleanup verified. CHK-130 [P1]: this iteration IS the security review. CHK-132 [P2]: path traversal blocked, temp files O_EXCL.

title: Symlink injection into store
disposition: Ruled out: O_NOFOLLOW on all opens, ISLNK check on base, dev/ino comparison

title: Path traversal escape
disposition: Ruled out: dir_fd anchoring prevents escape; no user-controlled paths

title: Unchecked ownership
disposition: Ruled out: secure_stat checks st_uid on all operations

title: TOCTOU between check and use
disposition: Ruled out for core ops: dir_fd anchoring + atomic rename + post-rename stat. Partial TOCTOU in advance() poison documented as P2-3-002.

title: Temp file residue after crash
disposition: Ruled out: write_json finally block + bounded cleanup

title: Cross-session record leakage
disposition: Ruled out: sha256(sessionId) isolation; no enumeration path
